status: Source, HTML export and page-loading review validated
implementation: Start likely page textures alongside initial scene loading. Use Cocos loadAny priority -1 for optional equipment textures; retain normal priority for shared chrome and the character page. Do not await optional page prewarm in world readiness, and do not repeat its inventory/catalog scan during map travel.

Split management-page art by usage, share in-flight texture requests, and retain each visited skill family with an explicit Node owner. Prepare only the current seven-skill family initially, rather than the full 33-skill catalog.

Overlap independent VFX shader variants, shield preparation, equipment effects, damage glyphs and combat audio. Keep the final rendered-frame/physics readiness gate and the existing frame-rate setting.

Keep the previous complete page during asynchronous preparation and place a transparent native BlockInputEvents guard above it. Show a compact shared gold-panel status only after 150ms; fast cache hits have no artificial delay. Release the guard on completion, failure, cancellation, authentication interruption and disposal; rebuild it on resize. Exclude it from title-menu HUD concealment.

method.host: Windows desktop Chrome, headless, same 844x390 viewport, DPR 3, touch emulation; HTML painted-world/native-hero mode
method.baseline: Retained pre-change concept-2d-audio export; inspected original page-prewarm and sequential shader code. World/economy work was also changing in the shared worktree, so these are local workflow samples, not an isolated whole-repository benchmark.
method.final: Fresh normal-rule concept-2d export at 127.0.0.1:7469, with final source. A new browser context per sample; one browser process per phase. No disk/OS/shader cache purge. First process sample includes more shader compilation than later contexts.
method.pageTiming: open() through asynchronous preparation and one completed render frame; normal level-one isolated session. Attributes, equipment, skills, forge, equipment, skills in that order.
method.travelTiming: Session enter and full scene rebuild into S01 and back to S01-T1; used as functional evidence. No map-transition speedup claimed.
limitations: Local server has no mobile download/decompression cost.
Small sample and non-identical unrelated world/economy changes; timing gains are illustrative local observations.
No physical Android device was attached to ADB. TapTap installation, subpackage caching and device startup/resume remain unverified.

measurements.tradeoff: First equipment and skill-page opens are about 20–31ms slower in these samples because optional art is no longer a global startup gate. The median complete startup-plus-six-page workflow is faster. Repeat opens are approximately 36–55ms, broadly similar to the retained build; no universal page-speedup percentage is claimed.
